    Tracking Project Progress with Task Output Quantities

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2353 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Measuring project progress accurately is essential for effective project financial management.
    • A project may consume a significant portion of its budget without achieving the corresponding level of physical progress.
    • For projects involving measurable deliverables, tracking physical work quantities provides another dimension of performance measurement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Measuring project progress accurately is essential for effective project financial management. While project managers regularly monitor budgets, actual costs, commitments, and forecasts, financial measures alone do not always provide a complete picture of how much work has been accomplished.

    A project may consume a significant portion of its budget without achieving the corresponding level of physical progress. Similarly, a task may be progressing efficiently even when its expenditure pattern differs from the original proposal.

    For projects involving measurable deliverables, tracking physical work quantities provides another dimension of performance measurement.

    With Oracle Fusion Cloud Project Management Revision 26D, the Track Progress with Task Output Quantities feature introduces capabilities for planning, capturing, and analyzing measurable work quantities against financial project tasks.

    The functionality enables project managers to define expected output, record completed quantities, calculate physical progress, and evaluate productivity using planned and actual performance measures.

    This article explores the functional capabilities, configuration requirements, productivity measures, and integration considerations associated with task output quantities in Oracle Fusion Cloud PPM.

    Task output quantities, also referred to as work quantities, represent measurable units of work associated with project activities.

    Unlike financial measures that indicate how much money has been spent, output quantities describe the physical work planned or completed.

    For example, construction and engineering projects may measure progress through installed pipeline lengths, concrete volumes, or other quantifiable deliverables.

    The objective is to establish a measurable relationship between the work expected and the work actually performed.

    In Oracle Fusion Cloud Project Management, output quantities can be maintained against the lowest-level tasks in the financial project strategy.

    Each applicable task can have a planned output quantity and an associated unit of measure.

    As work progresses, actual output quantities can be captured through project progress entry.

    These quantities provide a basis for calculating physical percent complete and reviewing productivity.

    This introduces a more objective method of evaluating task progress where the work can be measured in consistent units.

    Project progress is often assessed through schedule milestones, cost consumption, or manually entered completion percentages.

    These approaches remain useful, but they may not always reflect the actual volume of work delivered.

    Cost consumption indicates the financial resources used, while physical progress indicates the quantity of work completed.

    The two measures answer different questions.

    Financial progress: How much of the available financial resources has been consumed?

    Physical progress: How much of the planned work has actually been completed?

    Tracking both provides a more complete understanding of project performance.

    When output quantities are available, project managers can compare physical accomplishments with the resources consumed to achieve them.

    This supports a more meaningful evaluation of productivity and helps identify potential differences between planned and actual performance.

    For organizations managing projects with measurable deliverables, this capability can strengthen progress reporting and financial oversight.

    The first step is defining the expected physical output for the applicable financial project tasks.

    Oracle supports planned output quantities at the lowest level of the financial task structure.

    The planned quantity represents the expected amount of measurable work associated with the task.

    A corresponding unit of measure identifies how the output is quantified.

    Together, these attributes establish the planned physical scope against which actual progress can be evaluated.

    Output quantities are defined against lowest-level financial tasks.

    This is an notable design consideration because the financial task hierarchy may contain summary tasks and detailed execution tasks.

    The lowest-level tasks represent the detailed activities against which the measurable work is planned and tracked.

    When configuring the financial project proposal, project managers should ensure that the task structure supports the required level of progress measurement.

    The unit of measure provides the basis for interpreting the planned and actual quantities.

    For quantity-based progress to be meaningful, the output must be measured consistently.

    The planned quantity and recorded progress should therefore represent the same type of physical work.

    This consistency is essential when evaluating task completion and productivity.

    Once the planned output quantity has been established, actual completed quantities can be recorded through project progress entry.

    This allows project managers to track the physical work delivered against the planned quantity.

    The captured actual output provides a measurable basis for evaluating progress.

    Rather than relying exclusively on a manually estimated completion percentage, the system can use completed output quantities to calculate physical percent complete.

    To enable quantity-based physical progress calculation, select:.

    Physical Percent Complete Calculation Method: Output Units.

    This selection must be made for the lowest-level task.

    With this method, physical progress is calculated using the relationship between actual completed output and planned output.

    Conceptually, the calculation can be represented as:.

    Physical Percent Complete = (Actual Output Quantity / Planned Output Quantity) × 100.

    This formula illustrates the underlying quantity-based measurement concept. The exact application behavior, including any validations or special conditions, should be confirmed during configuration and testing.

    Using completed quantities as the basis for physical progress provides a consistent measurement approach for tasks with quantifiable deliverables.

    One of the most valuable aspects of task output quantities is the ability to compare completed work with the corresponding resource input.

    Physical progress explains how much work has been accomplished.

    Productivity analysis goes further by evaluating the relationship between the output achieved and the resources consumed.

    This distinction is important for project managers responsible for monitoring execution efficiency.

    A task may be progressing according to its planned completion percentage while requiring more resources than originally anticipated.

    Similarly, another task may achieve the expected output with a different level of resource consumption.

    By reviewing output quantities alongside resource input, project managers can better understand how efficiently work is being performed.

    Oracle provides planned productivity, actual productivity, and a productivity index to support this analysis.

    The feature introduces three productivity-related measures that project managers can review.

    Planned productivity establishes the expected productivity benchmark.

    It connects the planned physical output with the resources expected to complete the work.

    This provides a reference point for evaluating execution performance.

    Actual productivity considers the completed output and corresponding actual resource input.

    It helps project managers understand the productivity achieved during execution.

    Comparing actual productivity with the planned benchmark can highlight differences between expected and realized performance.

    The productivity index provides a measure for comparing productivity performance.

    It helps project managers assess how actual productivity relates to the planned benchmark.

    The interpretation of the index should follow Oracle's delivered calculation and the applicable resource measurement basis.

    The supplied feature documentation confirms the availability of the productivity index but does not specify its calculation formula. Therefore, the precise formula should be verified in the application or detailed Oracle documentation rather than assumed.

    Oracle makes output quantity and productivity information available within existing project management pages.

    This allows project managers to review the measures in the context of the financial project proposal and progress information.

    The Manage Financial Project Blueprint page supports the planning and review of task output quantities.

    The relevant output quantity and productivity columns are hidden by default.

    This configuration allows project managers to review the measures alongside the relevant financial planning information.

    The Manage Resources dialog box provides visibility into productivity measures.

    Project managers can review planned productivity, actual productivity, and the productivity index in the context of resource information.

    This is particularly relevant when evaluating the relationship between physical work delivered and the resources used.

    The Progress tab of the Manage Financial Project Plan page also provides access to output quantity and productivity information.

    This allows project managers to review completed quantities and related performance measures during progress tracking.

    Together, these locations support planning, progress capture, and productivity review within the project management workflow.

    Physical output quantities can also provide useful information for project financial processes.

    For projects where billing arrangements are linked to measurable work, completed quantities can support the determination of billable progress.

    Similarly, reliable progress information can contribute to financial analysis and revenue-related processes where the applicable business rules use physical completion measures.

    However, capturing output quantities does not automatically establish a particular billing or revenue recognition method.

    The actual financial treatment depends on the project's contract terms, billing configuration, revenue recognition rules, and related Oracle Fusion Cloud setup.

    From a functional perspective, the benefit is that measurable work progress becomes available as structured project information.

    This can support more consistent financial evaluation when quantity-based information is relevant to the business process.

    Oracle supports loading relevant output quantity and productivity information through File-Based Data Import (FBDI).

    This is key for organizations where project planning or progress information originates outside Oracle Fusion Cloud.

    The supported FBDI processes include:.

    The specific attributes available through each import should be confirmed against the applicable FBDI template and Oracle documentation.

    In many project environments, physical progress information may be captured through external planning, engineering, or project execution applications.

    FBDI support provides a mechanism for loading supported information into Oracle Fusion Cloud.

    This can help organizations incorporate output quantity tracking into their existing integration architecture.

    However, integration design should account for data ownership, unit-of-measure consistency, task identification, and the timing of progress updates.

    These considerations are important for maintaining reliable quantity-based progress information.

    In addition to FBDI, Oracle provides REST API support for loading and retrieving supported output quantity and productivity values.

    The relevant REST API areas are:.

    This extends the integration options available to organizations using external project management or execution systems.

    REST APIs can support application-to-application interactions where supported project planning or progress information needs to be exchanged.

    From an integration perspective, the choice between FBDI and REST APIs should depend on the intended processing model, transaction volume, frequency, and supported attributes.

    FBDI may be suitable for structured file-based loads, while REST APIs provide an option for service-based integrations.

    The appropriate design should be validated against Oracle's supported operations and the organization's integration requirements.

    The functionality is delivered as an opt-in feature.

    Track Progress with Task Output Quantities.

    Use the Oracle Fusion Cloud Opt In user interface to enable the feature.

    The feature documentation identifies upgrade 27D as the release from which the feature is no longer optional.

    This means organizations planning adoption before that point should review the applicable opt-in requirements for their environment.

    After enablement, the relevant project planning and progress configuration should be reviewed to ensure that quantity-based progress measurement is available where required.

    There are two important application configuration steps identified in the feature documentation.

    On the Manage Financial Project Initiative page, the output quantity and productivity columns are hidden by default.

    Select the required columns to make the information visible.

    Without this step, users may not immediately see the newly available measures.

    For lowest-level tasks where physical percent complete should be calculated from completed output quantities, select:.

    Physical Percent Complete Calculation Method = Output Units.

    This configuration connects actual output quantity entry with the task's physical progress calculation.

    Consultants should confirm that the task structure, planned output quantity, and unit of measure are appropriate before adopting this method.

    The introduction of task output quantities creates several areas that deserve attention during solution design.

    Quantity tracking is supported at the lowest level of financial tasks.

    The project task structure should therefore reflect the level at which physical work needs to be measured.

    Planned and actual quantities must be meaningful when compared.

    A consistent measurement basis is essential for accurate progress analysis.

    The Output Units method must be selected for tasks where quantity-based physical percent complete is required.

    This should be included in the project planning and progress configuration review.

    Productivity measures should be evaluated in the context of the relevant resource input.

    The productivity index should not be interpreted without understanding the applicable calculation and measurement basis.

    Organizations using external systems to capture physical progress should review the supported FBDI and REST API attributes.

    Data validation, task mapping, and progress update frequency are important considerations.

    Where output quantities are intended to support billing or financial analysis, the relevant contract and financial configurations should be reviewed separately.

    Physical progress measurement and financial processing are related, but they are not interchangeable.

    Task output quantities provide an additional level of visibility into project execution.

    More objective progress measurement.

    Completed physical quantities provide a measurable basis for determining task progress.

    Comparing completed output with resource input helps project managers assess execution efficiency.

    Physical progress can be reviewed alongside project financial information, supporting a more complete understanding of project performance.

    Support for quantity-based billing requirements.

    Consistently captured output quantities can provide relevant information for billing processes where the contract and configuration support quantity-based treatment.

    Improved integration flexibility.

    FBDI and REST API support enable organizations to exchange supported output quantity and productivity information with external systems.

    More informed project management decisions.

    Planned and actual productivity measures help project managers identify areas that may require further investigation.

    These benefits are particularly relevant for projects where work progress can be measured through clearly defined physical quantities.

    The introduction of output quantities adds a measurable physical dimension to financial project planning and progress tracking.

    The significance of this enhancement lies in connecting planned work, completed work, and resource consumption.

    This provides a more structured basis for evaluating project execution performance.

    Tracking physical work quantities adds an important dimension to project progress management in Oracle Fusion Cloud PPM.

    While financial measures remain essential for understanding project expenditure and budget performance, they do not always indicate how much physical work has been completed.

    The Track Progress with Task Output Quantities feature addresses this by allowing project managers to proposal measurable output, capture completed quantities, calculate physical percent complete, and evaluate productivity against planned expectations.

    The availability of productivity measures in the financial project proposal and resource management pages also helps connect work accomplishment with resource consumption.

    From an Oracle PPM functional perspective, the feature is particularly relevant for organizations managing projects with measurable deliverables and a need for consistent progress reporting.

    Its value depends on appropriate task structure design, reliable quantity capture, consistent units of measure, and correct progress calculation configuration.

    With support for both FBDI and REST APIs, the capability can also be considered as part of broader project planning and progress integration solutions.

    Overall, task output quantities provide project managers with a more objective way to evaluate physical progress and a stronger foundation for productivity analysis.

    Refactoring Anxiety: 5 Cognitive Distortions That Sabotage Your Code Cleanup

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (810 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, you stare at the legacy module.
    • "What if I break something?" you think.
    • If this sounds familiar, you're not dealing with a technical problem — you're dealing with refactoring anxiety, a specific form of cognitive distortion that hits developers when facing legacy code.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, you stare at the legacy module. You know it needs refactoring. The tech debt is piling up, the bug reports are mounting, and every fresh feature takes twice as long as it should.

    But you can't bring yourself to touch it.

    "What if I break something?" you think. "What if I make it worse? Maybe I'm not smart enough to understand this code. Maybe I should just rewrite it from scratch.".

    If this sounds familiar, you're not dealing with a technical problem — you're dealing with refactoring anxiety, a specific form of cognitive distortion that hits developers when facing legacy code.

    Refactoring anxiety is the irrational fear that arises when a developer considers modifying existing code that "works but is a mess." It's not about the code itself — it's about the thoughts and beliefs you attach to the code.

    In Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), we learn that thoughts create feelings, not situations. The same legacy module that terrifies one developer is just "code to clean up" to another. The difference? The cognitive distortions running in the background.

    It has been revealed that the distortion: "This is fine for now. We'll refactor it in the next sprint.".

    According to recent reports, the reality: Tech debt compounds like financial debt. Every sprint you delay, the interest grows. The "next sprint" never comes because there's always something more urgent.

    Sources indicate that the CBT reframe: This is fortune telling + avoidance. You're predicting a future where you have time, which has never happened. Instead, ask: "What's the actual cost of not refactoring now?" Calculate the time spent on bugs + workarounds per week. Usually, the 2-hour refactor pays for itself in 2 weeks.

    The distortion: "The tests pass. It's working. Don't touch it.".

    Sources indicate that the reality: "Working" is a low bar. Code that "works" but is unreadable, untestable, or unmaintainable is a ticking time bomb. When it breaks (and it will), nobody will understand it.

    Recent findings suggest that the CBT reframe: This is mental filtering — you're focusing on "tests pass" while filtering out "nobody can maintain this." Ask: "What would a newly introduced dev need to change this code? If they can't, is it really working?".

    According to recent reports, the distortion: "I don't understand this code well enough. If I touch it, I'll introduce bugs.".

    In a recent development, the reality: This is imposter syndrome meeting catastrophizing. You're assuming you're not competent enough, and that any mistake will be catastrophic.

    Sources indicate that the CBT reframe: Ask: "What's the actual risk?" You have tests. You have version control. You have code review. The worst case is you revert a commit. That's not catastrophic — it's a Tuesday.

    Tool: Write a pre-refactoring thought record. List:.

    Recent findings suggest that the distortion: "This code is a mess. We should just rewrite it.".

    The reality: Rewrites are seductive but rarely the right choice. Joel Spolsky called it the single worst strategic mistake a software company can make. You're throwing away years of bug fixes, edge case handling, and institutional knowledge.

    The CBT reframe: This is all-or-nothing thinking — the code is either "perfect" or "garbage," with no middle ground. Ask: "Can I refactor one function? one module?" Incremental refactoring is boring, but it works. The "big rewrite" is emotional reasoning, not engineering.

    Sources indicate that the distortion: "I didn't write this. It's not my responsibility to fix it.".

    The reality: This is personalization gone in reverse. You're taking no responsibility, when in fact, any code you touch is now your responsibility. Leaving it broken is more irresponsible than fixing it.

    According to recent reports, the CBT reframe: Ask: "If I leave this, who will fix it? The next dev? Me in 6 months?" The answer is always "someone who has even less context than I do." That's not fair — to them, or to the codebase.

    Before you touch legacy code, take 5 minutes to write a pre-refactoring thought record:.

    This protocol takes 5 minutes and saves 5 hours of procrastination.

    Refactoring anxiety isn't about code — it's about cognitive distortions that make the task feel bigger than it is. The "We'll Fix It Later" Fallacy, the "I'll Make It Worse" Fear, the "Rewrite From Scratch" Urge — these are mental traps, not technical barriers.

    It has been revealed that the fix is a pre-refactoring thought record: identify the distortion, gather evidence, reframe, and proceed. Your code will thank you. Your anxiety will drop.

    It has been revealed that and that legacy module? It's not a monster. It's just code.

    Want to try the pre-refactoring thought record tool? The CBT Thought Record is free, works in your browser, and doesn't store your data.

    Part of the CBT for Developers series — practical cognitive behavioral therapy for developer anxiety, burnout, and imposter syndrome.

    Your Supplier Demanded $208 More After You Paid. Do Not Click Cancel.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1375 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the order went through.
    • In a recent development, read that ratio again.
    • This is not one bad seller being creative.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the order went through. The payment cleared. The supplier accepted it. Two days later, at 3:54 in the morning, a message arrives: due to price adjustments on the platform, your item requires an additional charge — in one documented October case, an extra $208 demanded on a motherboard that had just been bought on sale for €192.17, roughly €20 below its usual price of around €210.

    In a recent development, read that ratio again. The discount was €20. The surcharge demanded was more than ten times the discount, and more than the entire original purchase price. When the buyer refused, the reason changed within one exchange: first it was a platform price adjustment, then it was a pricing error discovered after the order was placed. The offer that followed is the tell — the seller would create a separate link to cover the difference. Not an adjustment to the original order. A second, separate payment, alongside it, outside the protection the original order carries.

    This is not one bad seller being creative. A 2026 margin-defense guide from TS Scout describes post-checkout price increases as a recurring operational risk, driven by tariff stacking, currency swings, and the end of duty-free low-value shipping. Your job in the first reply is to avoid the one click that makes it cost you twice.

    According to recent reports, the most useful sentence in that documented case came from the seller's own side. After the buyer pushed back, the seller admitted, in writing: under platform policies, sellers cannot unilaterally change the price or demand extra payment after an order is placed and paid for. That admission was followed by a "however" — the error was supposedly genuine, shipping at the original price was therefore impossible, and the only solution was to cancel.

    It has been revealed that both halves matter. The first half is your leverage: a paid order is a contract at the paid price, and a demand for extra payment after payment is a policy violation, not a negotiation you are obliged to join. The second half is the trapdoor: if shipping truly will not happen, the order will end — and how it ends is recorded very differently depending on who ends it.

    It has been revealed that if the seller cancels, or the shipping deadline passes with nothing sent, the platform records it as the seller's failure — transaction non-fulfilment, graded by severity, earning points that affect the seller's account and the shop's visibility. If the buyer requests the cancellation, it is recorded as a buyer-side cancellation. The seller clicks approve, the refund is prompt, and nothing is left in their statistics.

    According to recent reports, that asymmetry is why the conversation so often ends with a helpful offer: "I can assist you with the cancellation process, or you may initiate a cancellation request from your order details. We will approve it immediately." The seller is not being kind. They are asking you to absorb their non-fulfilment into your click, so their record stays clean for the next buyer. Your refund arrives either way. Their penalty only arrives if you do not volunteer.

    Industry observers note that for a dropshipper the stakes are doubled, because behind your supplier order sits your customer order. While you spend three days negotiating a surcharge, your own delivery promise is burning, and under the U.S. FTC's 30-day rule the duty to ship on time, notify delays, and offer cancellation with a prompt refund belongs to your store — "my supplier held the order hostage" explains the delay to your customer, but it does not transfer the obligation.

    Sources indicate that step 1: Do not pay the difference, and do not cancel. Reply in the order thread, in writing. One short message does the work: the order was placed and paid at the agreed price; platform policy does not allow a unilateral price change or extra payment after payment; please ship the order as paid, or confirm in this thread that you cannot fulfil it. Every word stays inside the platform's messaging, attached to the order, where a dispute reviewer can read it later. Never move this conversation to WhatsApp or email, and never pay a separate "difference link" — a second payment outside the original order is the hardest money to recover.

    In a recent development, step 2: Archive your evidence while it is fresh. Screenshot the order confirmation showing the item, the exact variant, the price paid, and the shipping terms, plus the seller's surcharge message with its timestamp. If you priced your store from this listing, save the listing as it looked when you ordered. This takes four minutes on day two and is nearly impossible to reconstruct on day twenty, when the listing has been edited and the message thread is buried. Sellers who win these disputes are usually just the ones who kept the receipts in order.

    In a recent development, step 3: Let the clock work for you, not against you. If the seller will not ship, the shipping deadline passing unshipped is their non-fulfilment, recorded against them — that record is part of your leverage, and it evaporates the moment you click cancel yourself. What you should do with the waiting time is protect your own customer: check whether a backup supplier can fulfil inside your promised window, and if not, send your customer the delay notice with a revised date or a full-refund option early, while it is still a choice you are offering rather than an apology you are making.

    Sources indicate that step 4: If the order dies, open the dispute from the order, with the thread attached. The seller's own admission, the surcharge demand, and your refusal are all in the order messages. File within the platform's protection window rather than accepting an off-platform refund promise, and state the outcome you want plainly: full refund of the amount paid on the original order. Then log the incident against the supplier — one surcharge demand is a data point, a second one is a sourcing decision, and the log is what turns "this seller felt shaky" into a number you can route around.

    Industry observers note that step 5: Set a margin ceiling before the next incident. Decide in advance the most you would ever pay a backup supplier to save an order at the original promise — and that the answer to a post-payment surcharge demand is always no, regardless of size. A $3 "small adjustment" paid once teaches the pattern that your store pays. The sellers who get repeated demands are, disproportionately, the ones who paid the first small one.

    Handled the offered way: the buyer clicks cancel, gets €192 back promptly, and feels the story is over. The seller's record shows a buyer-side cancellation — clean — and the practice continues because it cost them nothing. A dropshipper in that seat also lost three days of their customer's delivery window, with no record anywhere that the supplier failed.

    Handled the playbook way: the buyer refuses in the order thread, archives the confirmation and the demand, and waits. The seller either ships at the paid price — which happens more often than the opening message suggests, once the cancellation will clearly be theirs — or lets the deadline pass, takes the non-fulfilment record, and the dispute refunds the original payment with the full thread as evidence. Same refund if it fails. Completely different record.

    It has been revealed that A post-payment surcharge demand is not a pricing problem; it is a records problem wearing a pricing costume. The price was settled when you paid. Do not pay a separate difference link, do not move the conversation off the order thread, and above all do not click the cancellation that converts the seller's failure into your request. Reply once, in writing, archive everything, protect your own customer in parallel, and let the deadline assign the failure to the party that caused it.

    Has a supplier ever asked you for extra money after you paid? Tell me the amount and what you did — the patterns in the comments are usually worth more than any single guide.

    — Jinguo, maker of GetDropFlow (https://getdropflow.com).

    #23441. A correct webhook handler that still caused duplicate emails

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (251 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dev ↗ Open Full Page

    A correct webhook handler that still caused duplicate emails

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (251 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Our webhook handler did everything inline: verify the signature, enhancement the order, send the receipt email, push to the ERP, then return 200.
    • Recent findings suggest that the gateway's delivery timeout was 5 seconds.
    • Industry observers note that the fix was boring.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Our webhook handler did everything inline: verify the signature, enhancement the order, send the receipt email, push to the ERP, then return 200. On a normal day that took 300 ms. During an ERP slowdown it took 9 seconds.

    Recent findings suggest that the gateway's delivery timeout was 5 seconds. So every event during the slowdown was marked failed on their side, even though we had processed it. They retried on their schedule, we processed it again, and the receipt email went out twice for about 1,200 orders. The retries added load to an already slow ERP, which made the next handler slower. A small feedback loop.

    Industry observers note that the fix was boring. The handler now verifies the signature, writes the raw event to a table with a unique constraint on event_id, and returns 200. A separate worker reads the table and does the side effects. Ack time dropped to about 15 ms and stayed flat while the ERP was slow.

    According to recent reports, two things we only noticed afterwards. The gateway docs listed the timeout in a different section from the retry schedule. And our dashboards tracked handler errors but not handler latency, so nothing looked broken while it was happening.

    It has been revealed that how do you monitor webhook ack latency? Do you alert on p99 against the sender's timeout, or only on error rate?

    Payneteasy handles this kind of payment flow for merchants and PSPs — see how it works.

    📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Choosefi

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that what's your FI number?
    • Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.
    • Industry observers note that "Is Social Security taxable?" is one of the most common tax questions retirees ask — and the answer frustrates almost everyone: it depends.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that what's your FI number? Calculate it in 60 seconds.

    The one number that changes everything.

    Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

    Industry observers note that "Is Social Security taxable?" is one of the most common tax questions retirees ask — and the answer frustrates almost everyone: it depends. Depending on your total income, anywhere from 0% to 85% of your Social Security benefits can be subject to federal income tax. The tax was introduced in 1983, originally affecting about 10% of recipients. Today, because the income thresholds were never indexed for inflation, roughly 56% of Social Security recipients pay tax on their benefits.

    Industry observers note that the good news: even in the worst case, you'll never pay tax on 100% of your Social Security. The bad news: the formula for calculating the taxable amount is one of the most convoluted in the entire tax code. In this guide, we'll break it down into plain English, show you exactly how to calculate what you owe, and — most importantly — share strategies the FI community uses to reduce or eliminate the tax entirely.

    According to recent reports, the IRS uses a special formula called "combined income" (also called "provisional income") to determine how much of your Social Security benefits are taxable. Here's the formula:.

    Combined Income = Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) + Nontaxable Interest + Half of Social Security Benefits.

    Recent findings suggest that the resulting number determines which taxation tier you fall into. Notice that the thresholds haven't changed since 1993 — they are not adjusted for inflation, which means more retirees cross into taxable territory every year.

    Crucial: "Up to 85% taxed" does not mean you pay an 85% tax rate. It means 85% of your benefits are added to your taxable income and taxed at your ordinary income rate. If you're in the 22% bracket and 85% of your $30,000 benefit is taxable, you'd owe 22% on $25,500 — roughly $5,610.

    This is the most common Social Security tax confusion. When the IRS indicates "up to 85% of benefits are taxable," it means 85% of your benefit amount gets added to your taxable income and taxed at your regular rate. If your marginal rate is 22% and 85% of your $30,000 benefit is taxable, you owe about $5,610 — not $25,500. The effective tax rate on your full benefit in this example is about 18.7%.

    Let's walk through a real example. Meet Sarah: she's 67, single, retired, and receives $24,000 per year in Social Security benefits. She also has $18,000 in IRA withdrawals and $2,000 in municipal bond interest.

    Step 1: Calculate Combined Income.

    According to recent reports, step 2: Determine the Tier Sarah is single with combined income of $32,000, which falls between $25,000 and $34,000. She's in the 50% tier — up to 50% of her benefits may be taxable.

    It has been revealed that step 3: Calculate the Taxable Amount The actual calculation involves comparing two formulas and taking the lesser amount. For the 50% tier:.

    It has been revealed that sarah adds $3,500 to her other taxable income. At a 12% marginal rate, that's roughly $420 in additional federal tax on her Social Security.

    Beyond federal taxes, 13 states also tax Social Security benefits to some degree as of 2026. Each state has its own thresholds and exemption amounts:.

    The remaining 37 states and Washington, D.C. do not tax Social Security benefits at all. If you're planning where to retire, this is a meaningful factor — especially if you have substantial SS benefits combined with other retirement income.

    The FI community has identified several strategies that can significantly reduce the tax bite on Social Security benefits. The key insight: since taxation is based on combined income, controlling your income in retirement is the lever.

    Industry observers note that this is the single most powerful strategy. Roth IRA withdrawals are not included in the combined income formula. If you retire early (before Social Security age), you have a window of low-income years to convert Traditional IRA/401(k) money to Roth.

    In a recent development, example: Between ages 55 and 67, you convert $500,000 from your Traditional IRA to a Roth — paying tax at rates as low as 10-12%. When you claim Social Security at 67, your Roth withdrawals don't push you into a higher SS taxation tier. Instead of 85% of your benefits being taxable, you might pay tax on 0-50%.

    Recent findings suggest that the math is dramatic over a 25+ year retirement. Converting at 12% during early retirement to avoid 22%+ taxation on Social Security for decades produces enormous tax savings.

    Every dollar of AGI pushes you toward the 50% or 85% taxation tiers. Strategic levers include:.

    It has been revealed that once you reach age 70.5, you can donate up to $105,000 per year directly from your IRA to a qualified charity. This satisfies your Required Minimum Distribution (RMD) without the distribution being included in your AGI. Lower AGI means lower combined income, which means less Social Security is taxable.

    For charitably inclined retirees, QCDs are one of the most tax-efficient giving strategies available — they simultaneously reduce your income tax AND reduce the tax on your Social Security benefits.

    In a recent development, delaying Social Security from 62 to 70 increases your benefit by roughly 77%. But there's a secondary benefit: during the delay years, you have more room to do Roth conversions at low tax rates without Social Security benefits adding to your combined income. The combination of larger benefits and lower taxation on those benefits makes delay doubly powerful for tax optimization.

    If you retire before claiming Social Security, you have a golden window for Roth conversions. With little or no earned income and no SS benefits, you can convert Traditional IRA money to Roth at the lowest tax brackets of your lifetime. Every dollar you convert is a dollar that will never increase the tax on your Social Security benefits. This window closes permanently once you start claiming.

    A step-by-step walkthrough for estimating what you owe.

    List your AGI from all sources: IRA/401(k) withdrawals, pension income, wages, dividends, capital gains, rental income. Get your total Social Security benefit from your SSA-1099 form.

    Pro tip: Don't forget nontaxable municipal bond interest — it counts in the combined income formula even though it's not on your 1040.

    Recent findings suggest that add your AGI + nontaxable interest + half of your Social Security benefits. This "combined income" number determines your taxation tier.

    Compare your combined income to the thresholds: Single — $25K (50% tier), $34K (85% tier). Married filing jointly — $32K (50% tier), $44K (85% tier).

    According to recent reports, for the 50% tier: take 50% of combined income above the lower threshold (capped at 50% of benefits). For the 85% tier: the calculation is more complex — use IRS Publication 915 worksheet or tax software.

    Pro tip: Tax software handles this automatically. If doing it by hand, IRS Publication 915 has the complete worksheet.

    The taxable portion of your Social Security gets added to your other taxable income and taxed at your marginal rate. Check if your state also taxes Social Security.

    For single filers, Social Security becomes partially taxable when combined income exceeds $25,000 (50% tier) and up to 85% taxable above $34,000. For married filing jointly, the thresholds are $32,000 (50% tier) and $44,000 (85% tier). These thresholds have not changed since 1993 and are not indexed for inflation.

    It has been revealed that no. Social Security benefits are not earned income. They are classified as unearned income for tax purposes. This distinction matters for things like the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC), IRA contribution eligibility, and the Social Security earnings test (which only applies to earned income like wages and self-employment).

    No — and this is why Roth accounts are so powerful in retirement. Roth IRA withdrawals are not included in the combined income formula used to determine Social Security taxation. Converting Traditional IRA money to Roth before claiming Social Security can dramatically reduce the tax on your benefits for life.

    It has been revealed that yes. File Form W-4V with the Social Security Administration to have federal income tax withheld from your benefits. You can choose 7%, 10%, 12%, or 22% withholding. This avoids the surprise of a large tax bill at filing time. State tax withholding varies by state.

    Sources indicate that social Security benefits are included in the Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) calculation that determines Medicare Part B and Part D premium surcharges (IRMAA). High-income retirees can pay significantly more for Medicare — up to 3.4 times the standard premium. Managing MAGI in retirement affects both Social Security taxation and Medicare costs.

    Recent findings suggest that there have been numerous proposals to reform Social Security taxation, including indexing the thresholds for inflation, raising the taxable percentage above 85%, or eliminating the tax entirely. As of 2026, no changes have been enacted. The thresholds have remained unchanged since 1993, meaning inflation automatically pushes more retirees into taxable territory each year.

    Yes, Social Security benefits can be taxable — up to 85% of your benefits may be added to your taxable income depending on your combined income. The thresholds are low ($25,000 single, $32,000 married) and haven't been adjusted for inflation since 1993, catching more retirees every year. The single most powerful strategy is Roth conversions during early retirement years before claiming Social Security. Every dollar in a Roth account is a dollar that won't push your Social Security into the taxable zone. Blueprint your retirement income sources deliberately, and you can reduce or eliminate this tax entirely.

    Latest Update: Astro + Cloudflare Pages vs WordPress - A Technical Comparison for Modern Static Sites

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1582 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, in 2026, many teams still default to WordPress when building blogs or marketing sites, often without fully considering the architectural alternatives.
    • Modern visitors now expect lightning-fast page loads and perfect Core Web Vitals a bar that traditional WordPress setups struggle to meet without extensive optimization and caching strategies.
    • Industry observers note that this article examines why, for many developer-managed websites, Astro + Cloudflare Pages delivers superior results in performance, SEO, security, and maintainability compared to traditional WordPress deployments.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, in 2026, many teams still default to WordPress when building blogs or marketing sites, often without fully considering the architectural alternatives. The classic WordPress setup PHP on shared hosting or managed WordPress platforms, coupled with a MySQL database and a plugin ecosystem works reliably but comes with inherent performance trade-offs.

    Modern visitors now expect lightning-fast page loads and perfect Core Web Vitals a bar that traditional WordPress setups struggle to meet without extensive optimization and caching strategies.

    Industry observers note that this article examines why, for many developer-managed websites, Astro + Cloudflare Pages delivers superior results in performance, SEO, security, and maintainability compared to traditional WordPress deployments. We'll explore the technical trade-offs and help you make an informed decision for your next blog or business website.

    It has been revealed that astro is a modern web framework that prioritizes delivering fast, lightweight content by default. Instead of running client-side JavaScript on every page load, Astro generates complete HTML during build time. Only interactive elements—dubbed "islands of interactivity"—run JavaScript, and only when needed.

    Cloudflare Pages is a globally distributed static hosting platform that leverages Cloudflare's edge network for content delivery. Think of it as Git combined with Cloudflare's CDN and security stack with integrated CI/CD, zero-downtime deployments, and automatic edge caching.

    You write your content and components using Astro's Markdown, MDX, or frameworks Astro builds your site to static HTML during your CI/CD pipeline Cloudflare Pages takes the built static assets and deploys them to edge locations worldwide Every request hits the nearest edge location, serving cache-optimized HTML directly.

    This contrasts sharply with WordPress, which typically involves:.

    PHP processing on every request Database queries to fetch content Server-side template rendering Dynamic page generation per visitor.

    The result: WordPress delivers pages via server-side rendering, while Astro + Cloudflare Pages delivers pages via edge-based static serving.

    Astro sites start with a clean slate: static HTML by default. This means:.

    Zero JavaScript by default – Pages load instantly with just HTML Minimal HTTP requests – Bundles are eliminated from the initial response Small page weight – Often under 50KB for content pages Instant first paint – No rendering blockers.

    Real-world tests and case studies consistently show Astro sites achieving near-perfect Lighthouse performance scores. The initial page load times typically range from 0.5s to 1.5s for content-heavy sites, compared to 2s to 5s for typical WordPress installations.

    WordPress usually involves several performance bottlenecks:.

    PHP rendering on every request – Server-side template processing delays first byte Database queries – MySQL lookups add tens to hundreds of milliseconds Plugin overhead – Even maintenance plugins add significant JavaScript and processing Theme scripts – Most themes include jQuery and other bloat by default.

    These differences translate directly into Core Web Vitals:.

    LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) – Astro typically achieves under 1.5s, while WordPress often lands between 2-3s without extensive caching CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) – Astro's static nature means predictable layouts. WordPress experiences frequent layout shifts during dynamic content loading FID (First Input Delay) – Lower JavaScript payloads in Astro mean better interactivity FCP (First Contentful Paint) – Static HTML delivers content instantly, while WordPress waits for PHP to parse and render.

    The performance gap becomes more pronounced on mobile networks and in regions far from hosting servers. Since Cloudflare Pages serves content from their global edge network, the geographic distance factor disappears entirely.

    Static HTML serves SEO exceptionally well because:.

    Fast pages are prioritized by Google – Poor Core Web Vitals directly impact rankings Simple, crawlable markup – Search engines can parse clean HTML instantly without JavaScript Predictable content delivery – Same markup for all visitors regardless of device or traffic source.

    WordPress's JavaScript-heavy pages force Googlebot to execute JavaScript a process that's become more sophisticated but still less reliable than serving static HTML.

    Astro offers granular control over SEO elements:.

    Content collections and frontmatter provide structured data management:.

    Astro integrates seamlessly with popular SEO tooling:.

    Robots.txt generation via Astro's sitemap integration Structured data through @astrojs/sitemap and JSON-LD Meta tags automatically generated from frontmatter Image optimization via @astrojs/image, supporting WebP, lazy loading, and responsive sizes.

    Cloudflare Pages provides several SEO-specific benefits:.

    Global CDN distribution – Pages serve from 280+ edge locations Zero-Time to First Byte (TTFB) – Edge caching eliminates server latency Built-in SSL/HTTPS – No mixed content warnings Automatic performance optimization – Image compression, HTML minification.

    These factors combine to create a superior SEO foundation where pages load in under 500ms with perfect Core Web Vitals, immediately signaling relevance to search engines.

    The combination of fast performance, clean HTML, and reliable crawling translates to:.

    Faster indexing – Pages crawled and ranked immediately Higher visibility – Better Core Web Vitals improve rankings Better user engagement – Faster pages reduce bounce rates and increase dwell time Improved Zero-Click Searches – Perfect page structure for featured snippets and search features.

    Modern developer workflows prioritize speed and reliability:.

    Commit → Deploy – Automatic deployments directly from git branches Zero infrastructure management – No cPanel, FTP, or server administration Consistent environments – Same code runs identically across dev, staging, and prod Version control for content – Content is text files, fully version-controlled.

    Traditional WordPress workflows involve:.

    Content management through admin dashboard – HTML editors, plugin dependencies Theme and plugin management – Version control challenges for non-developers Performance tuning – Caching plugins, database optimization, CDN integration Security maintenance – Regular updates, vulnerability patches, backup systems.

    The WordPress approach demands significant operational overhead to achieve acceptable performance, while Astro + Cloudflare Pages delivers optimal performance by design.

    Astro + Cloudflare Pages: Only pay for Cloudflare usage ($5-20/month for hobby initiative, $20-100+ for pro tier) WordPress: Hosting ($10-50/month) + Premium plugins/themes ($20-100+/year) + Maintenance costs.

    In a recent development, performance is critical? → Astro + Cloudflare Pages Non-technical content creators needed? → WordPress Complex dynamic features required? → WordPress Budget is a primary concern? → Astro + Cloudflare Pages Developer-first approach preferred? → Astro + Cloudflare Pages Existing WordPress investment? → Consider WordPress (but evaluate migration ROI).

    **For most modern developer-managed projects, especially blogs, documentation sites, and marketing pages:.

    Total Cost: ~60-70% less with Astro + Cloudflare Pages Performance: Significantly better (0.5s vs 2-5s load times) Maintainability: Much easier (CI/CD vs ongoing administration) Security: Stronger (no database, fewer attack vectors) Developer Experience: Superior (modern toolchain vs legacy admin).

    Choose WordPress when you need:.

    Sources indicate that A column rename can leave application queries referring to a name that no longer exists. A migration changes the database, but the application still needs a compatible change.

    Recent findings suggest that SH-PSCBS is my experimental tool for connecting those two sides. It detects PostgreSQL schema differences and prepares code repair proposals for review.

    The demo renames a column, highlights a SQL diff, runs pytest, and verifies an approved commit against a disposable local Git remote. Model responses are simulated, so no API key or Ollama installation is required for this example.

    Each detected change becomes an event. The workflow can need clarification, a correction, another validation attempt, or a human decision. LangGraph expresses those routes, while SQLite stores snapshots, event state, and decisions.

    Analysis identifies schema changes and code evidence. Planning uses Groq with read-only tools. Correction uses Ollama in an isolated project copy. Validation checks integrity and syntax and runs pytest in a network-isolated Docker container. Review compares the plan, diff, and results.

    Recent findings suggest that approval creates a commit on a separate branch only after the required checks. A separate publish command pushes that branch. The destination repository still needs review and merge.

    This is experimental and currently focuses on PostgreSQL and Python. The CLI uses Portuguese command names. A dropped column and an added column may indicate a rename, but that is an inference. Polling can miss short-lived changes. A green test suite only covers what the tests exercise.

    Groq receives relevant code and context for planning and review; generation uses Ollama. Review that data flow before monitoring private projects.

    Sources indicate that the repository includes an MIT license, architecture and usage guides, and a contribution guide. Feedback on ambiguous migrations, repair evaluation, and the first-run experience would help. Try the demo and report the smallest example that reproduces a problem.

    Industry observers note that affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

    In a recent development, an affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

    Industry observers note that affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers. Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

    Industry observers note that dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

    Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

    It has been revealed that smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile people by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a significant opportunity.

    According to recent reports, the best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

    An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

    Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

    Industry observers note that A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program. Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

    Sources indicate that because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

    Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

    If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

    Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

    Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns.     Phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

    HubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

    Sources indicate that when you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

    Acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include major brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and firm-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

    Sources indicate that marketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for newly introduced content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

    Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

    According to recent reports, yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

    It has been revealed that albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

    According to recent reports, albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

    #23419. 7 Best Chain Restaurant Roast Beef Sandwiches, According To Customer Reviews

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1554 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    7 Best Chain Restaurant Roast Beef Sandwiches, According To Customer Reviews

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1554 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that roast beef sandwiches are one of the most hearty and heartening meals there is.
    • According to the latest dedicated study on the subject, a 2019 survey by YouGov found that around 71% of adults across the country enjoyed roast beef sandwiches.
    • Roy Rogers was once famed for its roast beef sandwiches, and today, people still line up for them whenever they get to visit one of the nearly 40 remaining locations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that roast beef sandwiches are one of the most hearty and heartening meals there is. That's why we think this comfort food deserves to be served year-round, not just on those brisk, rainy days when fall-apart-tender beef on a toasted baguette can be the most delicious way to warm up. Luckily, these chains' roast beef sandwiches are widely praised for their taste, texture, and consistency, so you can be sure you're getting a good-quality meal whenever you'd like to try one.

    And you won't be alone when you do. According to the latest dedicated study on the subject, a 2019 survey by YouGov found that around 71% of adults across the country enjoyed roast beef sandwiches. That's one reason why the restaurants chosen for this list have the sandwich on the menu anytime you want it, and a few even overlap with the chains that have the best French dips. In the end, whatever place you choose to stop at will feed you well with homey, warm roast beef slices on toothsome bread.

    Roy Rogers was once famed for its roast beef sandwiches, and today, people still line up for them whenever they get to visit one of the nearly 40 remaining locations. While it's been in business since the late 1960s, the chain has massively downscaled from its height of almost 650 stores in the 1990s. But the roast beef remains consistently delicious, thanks to the USDA Top Inside Round Roast Beef being slow-cooked for hours for maximum tenderness.

    The sandwich has a hardcore fan base, who often say the beef here is tastier and juicier than other national competitors. One Reddit commenter stated, "Roy's Roast beef is much better than Arby's. It actually tastes like real roast beef." Online reviewers suggest using the chain's barbecue and horseradish sauces to complete the experience. It helps that many of the remaining locations are in Maryland, where you can always grab some Baltimore tiger sauce for any leftovers.

    It has been revealed that and customers are willing to accept the limited regional footprint of the restaurant, although they're still hoping for an overall comeback for the brand. Those lucky enough to have an open Roy Rogers nearby have reported being overjoyed at the discovery.

    Sources indicate that arby's is a nostalgic favorite for many people for a reason – the perfectly textured and easy-to-chew beef. The global fast food chain began operations in 1964 but has since circled the globe with over 3,500 locations without forgetting that fact. That's why the roast beef Arby's uses has had the same four ingredients since it opened — beef, water, salt, and sodium phosphates. The meat is slow-cooked before being thinly sliced and added to a toasted sesame seed bun the diner can customize however they'd like.

    People have called Arby's classic roast beef sandwiches their preferred fast food order, adding they rarely try anything else because the meal is so consistently good. Other fans have echoed that consistency is also what brings them back, with one person saying they've always enjoyed their items from the restaurant. A Facebook user posted about their first time trying Arby's, saying, "Tried Arby's roasted beef sandwich. It is pretty tender and flavorful. It's like a poor man's prime rib." And customers love that they can choose how much meat to have put on the sandwich, with some noting they've enjoyed half-pound versions, with and without cheddar sauce.

    The smallest chain on this list is a Missouri powerhouse that's crossed over into Illinois. Even though that means most people will have to travel a bit to reach the nearest Lion's Choice, fans say the trip will be worth it. That's because the chain's roast beef sandwiches are made from the top round cut and are roasted in-house for freshness. Then there's the firm's proprietary blend of seasoning that's used to finish off the beef after it moves to the bun. The gluten-free mix helps set the meal apart from competitors, just like the secret roasting method does.

    Sources indicate that fans of Lion's Choice are quick to recommend the establishment to newcomers, and those who've moved away look forward to the eatery being one of their first stops upon returning. Guests suggest getting extra seasoning on the beef, with some advising buyers to add cheese as well. The brand's horseradish sauce is also praised for being flavorful, although the beef is always the star of the show.

    Recent findings suggest that black Bear Diner is an up-and-coming chain operating almost 170 locations across 14 states at the time of writing. Founded in 1995, the brand is dedicated to making comfort foods that taste as if they came straight from the best cook in the family's kitchen. The restaurant's Pot Roast Melt is certainly living up to that expectation. The meal is made with jack and cheddar cheeses, grilled onions, horseradish aioli, and slowly simmered pot roast. The sandwich also comes with au jus and is served on garlic- and Parmesan-crusted sourdough bread for a bit of crunch.

    The melt gets consistent praise from customers, whether it's the diner's first time trying the sandwich or if they've come back just for another one. One Facebook user posted about the meal, saying, "Black Bear Diner knocked it out of the park with their Pot Roast Melt! Pot Roast, onion and cheesy goodness on grilled parmesan/garlic bread. On top of that – you get to dip it in au jus!" Others have called it yummy, delicious, and so good, cementing the elevated status of the sandwich for Black Bear Diner fans.

    It has been revealed that like Lion's Choice, Culver's is another Midwest favorite for beef sandwiches. But Culver's is a little different because it's one of the only fast food chains that serves shredded pot roast instead of sliced beef. That creates a big difference in the taste and texture of the premium chuck roast the brand uses, so it's no surprise that Culver's Pot Roast Sandwich is praised for its rich flavor and lack of fat. One person was so impressed with the meal that they made it their go-to item from the menu.

    Other diners point out the generous size of the sandwich, as well as how juicy and tender the meat is. Fans suggest adding gravy and/or grilled onions to finish off the sandwich, but barbecue sauce is another popular way to add spice to the roast. Some people add Swiss cheese and mushrooms, too, although you might need to eat it quickly to keep the bun intact.

    Firehouse Subs is one of the largest fast food sandwich franchises in the U.S., with over 1,300 stores. It started in the mid-1990s and has always been dedicated to making filling meals that each diner could customize exactly as they'd like. The large menu includes hot and cold subs, as well as in-house sides and desserts. One of the most popular hot sandwiches is the Smokehouse Beef & Cheddar Brisket, which fans praise for its melty cheddar cheese, strong beefy flavor, and the incredibly tender brisket.

    People agree that Firehouse Subs is a pricier option than many other sandwich shops, but the quality of the ingredients and the generous portions make up for the higher cost. One Facebook user said, "Trying Firehouse Subs for [the] first time. Large smokehouse beef and cheddar combo, with small fries. Pricier than Subway at $32.42, but bloody delicious!!" Others agree about the taste, saying the sandwich is one of their favorites and that they've had consistently good experiences eating one.

    In a recent development, portillo's is a Chicago-based chain that's best known for its Italian-style roast beef sandwiches, although there are several kinds of roast beef subs on the menu. Served either dipped in au jus or dry, the meaty Italian Beef Sandwiches have a nice kick of spice from the Italian peppers that come atop the layered protein. The meal is so sought after that the business ships kits nationwide to make the Italian beef sandwiches. The set comes with all the elements needed to re-create the meal at home, and it serves up to 10 people.

    In a recent development, reviewers note the hot peppers that come on the sub add a spicy crunch that works nicely with the richness of the juicy meat. One Facebook user posted about the item, saying, "...I had a Portillo's beef yesterday with hot and sweet peppers and dipped twice. It was a pretty darn good beef sandwich.".

    Like that Facebook poster, many fans prefer to have the sandwich dipped, saying the flavor is worth the extra napkins you'll need. Some people even make long drives just to visit the shop. And who could blame them? The hot beef Italian subs offer great taste and value for some of the most tender meat you'll find at any chain restaurant.

    To build a list of the best roast beef sandwiches, we first searched for chain restaurants with more than 24 locations that served the meal. We then looked through social media and message board posts and comments, user review sites, and professional reviews for each chain's roast beef. We ultimately chose the restaurants whose customers had praised the meal for its taste, value, and consistency across multiple platforms to be represented on this list.
